name: Phenom
desc: Develops an AI-based talent experience platform for recruiting, hiring, career sites and employee development at large employers.
markets: Large employers mainly in North America, with customers and offices in Europe and India.
rationale: HR-tech rivals such as Workday, UKG and Avature sponsor F1; B2B hospitality and enterprise brand awareness among HR buyers.

name: Scality
desc: Develops software-defined object and file storage software, RING and ARTESCA, for enterprises, telecoms and cloud providers.
markets: Offices in France, UK, US and Japan; enterprise and service-provider customers across Europe, North America and Asia.
rationale: Data-infrastructure rivals such as NetApp, VAST Data and Dell sponsor F1; B2B hospitality and technology showcase potential.

name: Weave
desc: Provides communication, scheduling, payments and phone software for small healthcare practices such as dental and optometry offices.
markets: Small healthcare practices in the United States and Canada; no verified expansion beyond North America.
rationale: US-focused small-business software with little need for global sponsorship; weak F1 fit beyond US race hospitality.
changed: Listed on the NYSE in 2021

name: Lansweeper
desc: Develops IT asset discovery and inventory software that scans networks to map hardware, software and users.
markets: Customers of all sizes worldwide, sold online and via partners, from its Belgian base with international offices.
rationale: IT-management rivals such as NinjaOne and ServiceNow sponsor F1; could use B2B hospitality to reach IT buyers.

name: Clarivate
desc: Provides research, patent, trademark and life-sciences data and analytics, including Web of Science and Derwent.
markets: Universities, governments, corporations and law firms worldwide, with major operations in the UK, US and Asia.
rationale: Global B2B information brand; F1 hospitality could reach corporate IP and pharma clients, but low consumer focus.
changed: Spun out of Thomson Reuters in 2016; listed via SPAC merger in 2019; acquired ProQuest in 2021

name: Semantix
desc: Provides a data platform, analytics and AI software and services to large companies in Latin America.
markets: Enterprise customers in Brazil and other Latin American countries; no verified expansion outside Latin America.
rationale: Regional B2B data company; Brazilian Grand Prix hospitality is possible but overall F1 fit is weak.
changed: Listed on Nasdaq via SPAC merger in 2022; current listing status not confirmed

name: Liquidnet
desc: Operates an institutional trading network for block trading of equities and fixed income for asset managers.
markets: Asset managers across dozens of markets in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Part of TP ICAP; any F1 deal would sit with the parent group; limited standalone brand need.
changed: Acquired by TP ICAP in 2021

name: Dashlane
desc: Sells password manager apps and browser extensions that store and autofill credentials for consumers and businesses.
markets: Consumers and businesses worldwide, mainly North America and Europe, with offices in New York, Paris and Lisbon.
rationale: Direct rivals 1Password and Keeper Security sponsor F1; consumer and business security brand with global marketing needs.

name: Encora
desc: Provides outsourced software engineering, cloud, data and AI development services to software companies and enterprises.
markets: Clients mainly in North America, served from delivery centres in Latin America, India and Europe.
rationale: IT-services peers such as Cognizant, Globant and Mphasis sponsor F1; useful for B2B hospitality with US clients.

name: Appier
desc: Provides AI-based marketing, advertising and customer data software that helps brands acquire and retain customers.
markets: Asia-Pacific core with Japan its largest market; has been expanding into the US and Europe.
rationale: Listed AI marketing company growing outside Asia; Japanese and Singapore Grand Prix hospitality could reach brand clients.
changed: Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange in 2021

name: Forcepoint
desc: Develops data security, cloud access security, web security and firewall software for enterprises and governments.
markets: Enterprise and government customers worldwide, with operations in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Cybersecurity rivals CrowdStrike, Zscaler and Cato Networks sponsor F1; enterprise brand with global B2B hospitality needs.
changed: Sold by Raytheon to Francisco Partners in 2021; government unit sold to TPG in 2023, now Everfox

name: Dixa
desc: Provides cloud customer service software combining phone, chat, email and messaging with AI routing and automation.
markets: Consumer-facing companies mainly in Europe, with some customers in North America.
rationale: Customer-experience rivals such as Salesforce and Genesys sponsor F1, but Dixa is small; plausible but modest fit.

name: Sprout Social
desc: Sells social media management software for publishing, engagement, listening and analytics to businesses and agencies.
markets: Business customers in about 100 countries, with offices in North America, Europe and Australia.
rationale: Marketing-software brand; F1 content and social reach offer showcase value; rivals like Salesforce and Adobe sponsor F1.

name: Powerfleet
desc: Provides IoT telematics devices and software to track and manage vehicles, trailers, containers and industrial equipment.
markets: Fleet and industrial customers in North America, Europe, Israel, South Africa, Latin America and other markets.
rationale: Logistics and fleet telematics fit F1's logistics story; B2B hospitality with transport and industrial customers.
changed: Merged with MiX Telematics in 2024; acquired Fleet Complete in 2024

name: Calix
desc: Supplies cloud software, broadband systems and managed services to broadband service providers serving homes and businesses.
markets: Broadband providers mainly in the United States and Canada, with a small number of international customers.
rationale: Sells to regional broadband operators; little need for global sponsorship; weak F1 fit.

name: NETSCOUT Systems
desc: Sells network performance monitoring, service assurance and DDoS protection products to telecom carriers, enterprises and governments.
markets: Carriers, enterprises and governments worldwide, with operations in North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Network and security rivals such as Cisco and Extreme Networks sponsor F1; B2B hospitality with carriers is plausible.
changed: Acquired Danaher's communications business in 2015

name: VeriSign
desc: Operates the authoritative registries for the .com and .net domains and runs two internet root servers.
markets: Registrars and domain holders worldwide; revenue comes from registry fees on .com and .net names.
rationale: Near-monopoly registry with little marketing need; brand-building sponsorship offers limited return; weak F1 fit.

name: SailPoint
desc: Develops identity security software to govern user access to applications, data and cloud resources for enterprises.
markets: Large enterprises and governments in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Identity rival Okta and other security firms sponsor F1; enterprise brand with global B2B hospitality value.
changed: Taken private by Thoma Bravo in 2022; re-listed on Nasdaq in 2025

name: Secureworks
desc: Provides managed detection and response, Taegis XDR software, incident response and threat intelligence services.
markets: Enterprises and public bodies in more than 50 countries, now within the Sophos group.
rationale: Now part of Sophos; any F1 deal would be decided by the parent; limited standalone marketing budget.
changed: Acquired by Sophos in 2025

name: AST SpaceMobile
desc: Builds a constellation of large low-earth-orbit satellites to provide cellular broadband directly to ordinary smartphones.
markets: Early stage: service agreements with mobile operators including AT&T, Verizon, Vodafone and Rakuten; full commercial service still rolling out.
rationale: Space technology showcase with operator partners; consumer-facing satellite service could use F1, but still pre-commercial.
changed: Listed via SPAC merger in 2021

name: SBA Communications
desc: Owns and leases wireless communication towers and sites to mobile network operators as a real estate investment trust.
markets: Towers in the United States, Canada, Central and South America and South Africa.
rationale: Infrastructure landlord serving a few carriers; no consumer brand; weak F1 fit.

name: Zayo Group
desc: Provides fibre-optic network infrastructure, dark fibre, wavelengths and connectivity to carriers, hyperscalers and enterprises.
markets: Carriers, hyperscalers and enterprises mainly in North America, with fibre operations also in Europe.
rationale: B2B infrastructure provider; hospitality with hyperscalers and carriers possible, but limited brand need.
changed: Taken private by DigitalBridge and EQT in 2020; agreed in 2025 to buy Crown Castle's fibre business

name: Cogeco
desc: Provides cable, internet, TV and phone services in Quebec, Ontario and the US, plus radio broadcasting.
markets: Residential and business subscribers in Quebec and Ontario, and in US states under the Breezeline brand.
rationale: Consumer brand in Quebec and Ontario; Canadian Grand Prix in Montreal offers local activation and hospitality.

name: Xplore
desc: Provides rural broadband internet by fibre, fixed wireless and satellite to homes and businesses in Canada.
markets: Homes and businesses in rural Canada only; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic rural broadband provider; Canadian Grand Prix is the only plausible angle; weak F1 fit.
changed: Acquired by Stonepeak in 2020; renamed from Xplornet to Xplore in 2022

name: FiberLight
desc: Builds and leases fibre-optic network infrastructure to carriers, enterprises, government agencies and data centres.
markets: Carriers, enterprises and government customers in several US states; no verified international activity.
rationale: Regional US wholesale fibre provider with no consumer brand; weak F1 fit.

name: Celero Communications
desc: Develops coherent DSP chips and optical connectivity products for data centre and telecom networks, per Crunchbase.
markets: Few public details; intended customers are network equipment makers and cloud providers; no verified international activity.
rationale: Early-stage B2B chip developer with little public profile and no consumer brand; weak F1 fit.

name: KORE Wireless
desc: Provides IoT cellular connectivity, connectivity management, devices and managed services for enterprise customers.
markets: Enterprise customers in healthcare, fleet, logistics and industry worldwide, with over 20 million connections.
rationale: B2B IoT provider; connected-car and telemetry themes give some technology tie-in, but modest brand need.
changed: Listed on NYSE via SPAC merger in 2021; Wikipedia now describes it as privately owned

name: Bandwidth
desc: Sells voice calling, messaging and emergency calling APIs over its own IP voice network to businesses.
markets: Enterprises and software firms mainly in the US, with network coverage and customers in Europe and other countries.
rationale: Communications API rivals such as Infobip and Cisco Webex sponsor F1; plausible B2B hospitality fit.
changed: Acquired Voxbone in 2020

name: Ribbon Communications
desc: Sells communications software, session border controllers and IP optical networking equipment to telecom carriers and enterprises.
markets: Carriers, enterprises and critical-infrastructure customers in North America, Europe, Asia and other regions.
rationale: B2B telecom vendor; hospitality with carriers possible, but limited brand need; plausible but not obvious.
changed: Formed by merger of Sonus Networks and Genband in 2017

name: Amphenol
desc: Makes electrical, electronic and fibre optic connectors, cables, antennas and sensors for many industries.
markets: Manufacturers in automotive, aerospace, data centre, mobile and industrial markets worldwide, with plants in many countries.
rationale: Large industrial group with automotive and data-centre exposure; technology tie-in possible, though brand marketing is limited.

name: Microchip Technology
desc: Designs and makes microcontrollers, analog chips, FPGAs, memory and security devices for industrial, automotive and other equipment.
markets: Equipment makers worldwide, sold directly and through distributors, with fabs and offices in the US, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Chip rivals AMD, Intel and Qualcomm sponsor F1; automotive and embedded technology tie-in with B2B hospitality.

name: onsemi
desc: Makes power and sensing semiconductors, including silicon carbide devices and image sensors, for automotive and industrial customers.
markets: Carmakers and industrial customers worldwide, with manufacturing in the US, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Car electrification chips give a clear automotive technology tie-in; chip rivals such as AMD and Intel sponsor F1.
changed: Renamed from ON Semiconductor to onsemi in 2021

name: Infineon Technologies
desc: Designs and makes power semiconductors, microcontrollers, sensors and security chips for cars, industry and data centres.
markets: Carmakers and manufacturers worldwide, with fabs in Germany, Austria and Asia and sales in all major regions.
rationale: Leading automotive chip supplier; technology showcase and hospitality with carmakers; chip rivals already sponsor F1.

name: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company
desc: Manufactures advanced logic chips under contract for chip designers such as Apple, Nvidia, AMD and Qualcomm.
markets: Chip design customers worldwide; fabs mainly in Taiwan, with plants in the US and Japan and one being built in Germany.
rationale: Foundry with few customers and little marketing need, though AI and technology showcase value is real.

name: Midea Group
desc: Makes home appliances, air conditioners, commercial HVAC and industrial robots under brands including Midea, Toshiba and KUKA.
markets: Consumers and businesses worldwide, with factories and subsidiaries across Asia, Europe and the Americas.
rationale: Global consumer appliance brand building awareness outside China; F1 offers mass consumer reach and hospitality.
changed: Listed in Hong Kong in 2024

name: NXP Semiconductors
desc: Designs and makes automotive processors, radar chips, secure identification and NFC chips, and industrial connectivity chips.
markets: Carmakers, device makers and industrial customers in more than 30 countries across Europe, Asia and the Americas.
rationale: Major automotive chip supplier; technology tie-in with racing electronics; chip rivals already sponsor F1.
changed: Spun out of Philips in 2006

name: Copeland
desc: Makes compressors, controls and software for heating, air conditioning, refrigeration and cold-chain systems.
markets: Equipment makers and contractors worldwide, with operations in North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: B2B industrial brand; sustainability and cooling technology story possible, but limited consumer marketing; plausible but not obvious.
changed: Carved out of Emerson in 2023 as Copeland under Blackstone ownership; Emerson sold its remaining stake in 2024

name: Columbus McKinnon
desc: Designs and makes hoists, cranes, rigging, chain and motion-control products for industrial and entertainment customers.
markets: Industrial, construction and entertainment customers in North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Industrial lifting brand with B2B customers; little consumer marketing; weak to modest F1 fit.
changed: Agreed in 2025 to acquire lifting-products maker Kito Crosby

name: Viavi Solutions
desc: Makes network test, measurement and assurance equipment and software, plus optical coatings for anti-counterfeiting.
markets: Telecom carriers, equipment makers, data centres and governments worldwide.
rationale: B2B test equipment brand; network technology angle possible, but limited marketing need; plausible but not obvious.
changed: Spun out of JDS Uniphase in 2015

name: Diodes Incorporated
desc: Designs and supplies discrete, analog and mixed-signal semiconductors for automotive, industrial, computing and consumer products.
markets: Electronics makers worldwide, with factories in Asia and the US and sales across Asia, Europe and North America.
rationale: Component supplier with little brand marketing; automotive chip angle only; weak to modest F1 fit.

name: Texas Instruments
desc: Designs and makes analog and embedded processing chips, and sells educational calculators.
markets: Industrial, automotive and electronics customers worldwide, with fabs mainly in the US.
rationale: Major chipmaker with automotive exposure; chip rivals already sponsor F1; technology and hospitality tie-in.

name: AMETEK
desc: Makes electronic instruments, sensors, motors and electromechanical devices for aerospace, medical, industrial and power markets.
markets: Industrial, aerospace and medical customers worldwide, with over 150 sites across many countries.
rationale: Diversified B2B instruments group with little consumer marketing; precision-engineering angle only; plausible but not obvious.

name: GlobalFoundries
desc: Manufactures specialty and mature-node semiconductors under contract for automotive, mobile, IoT, aerospace and data centre chips.
markets: Chip design customers worldwide, with fabs in New York, Vermont, Germany and Singapore.
rationale: Foundry with few large customers and limited brand need; Abu Dhabi ownership adds a Gulf hospitality angle only.
changed: Created from AMD's manufacturing arm in 2009; listed on Nasdaq in 2021

name: Hubbell Incorporated
desc: Makes electrical and utility products, including grid components, connectors and wiring devices, for utilities and buildings.
markets: Utility, industrial and construction customers mainly in the United States, with smaller operations abroad.
rationale: Mostly US utility and electrical supplier; little international brand need; weak F1 fit beyond US race hospitality.

name: Jabil
desc: Provides electronics manufacturing services, building products and components for data centre, healthcare, automotive and consumer companies.
markets: Brand-owner customers worldwide, with plants in over 30 countries across the Americas, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Contract manufacturer with little brand marketing; B2B hospitality with customers possible; plausible but not obvious.

name: Rapidus
desc: Developing 2-nanometre logic chip manufacturing in Chitose, Hokkaido, backed by Japanese companies and government funding.
markets: Pre-revenue: pilot production in Japan, with mass production targeted for 2027; customers not yet confirmed.
rationale: Pre-revenue foundry relying on state support; no brand to market yet; weak F1 fit.

name: Solstice Advanced Materials
desc: Makes refrigerants, electronic materials, fluorine chemicals and specialty materials for industrial, electronics and healthcare customers.
markets: Industrial and electronics customers worldwide, inherited from Honeywell's global specialty materials business.
rationale: New listed company building its own brand; low-emission refrigerants give a sustainability story; plausible but not obvious.
changed: Spun off from Honeywell in October 2025

name: TeamSystem
desc: Develops accounting, payroll, e-invoicing and management software for small businesses, accountants and professionals.
markets: Mainly Italy, with operations also in Spain and other European countries.
rationale: Italian software brand; Monza and Imola hospitality could reach SME and accountant customers; plausible fit.

name: Micron Technology
desc: Designs and makes DRAM, high-bandwidth memory, NAND flash and SSDs for data centres, devices and vehicles.
markets: Data-centre, PC, phone, automotive and industrial customers worldwide, with fabs in the US, Japan, Taiwan and Singapore.
rationale: Memory supplier for AI and automotive; chip rivals sponsor F1; technology showcase and hospitality value.
changed: Announced exit from the Crucial consumer business in 2025

name: Command Alkon
desc: Provides dispatch, ticketing, ordering and logistics software for ready-mixed concrete, aggregates and asphalt producers.
markets: Concrete, aggregates and asphalt producers mainly in North America, with customers in Europe and other regions.
rationale: Niche B2B software vendor to building materials producers; little brand need; weak F1 fit.

name: indie Semiconductor
desc: Designs automotive chips and modules for driver assistance, radar, lidar, in-cabin sensing and connectivity.
markets: Carmakers and Tier-1 suppliers, with engineering in the US, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Automotive-focused chipmaker; ADAS technology tie-in with racing, but small marketing budget; plausible fit.
changed: Listed via SPAC merger in 2021

name: Innoviz Technologies
desc: Develops lidar sensors and perception software for driver assistance and autonomous driving in passenger vehicles.
markets: Carmakers and suppliers in Europe and other regions, from its Israeli base with offices abroad.
rationale: Automotive sensing technology fits a racing showcase, but small company with limited budget; plausible fit.
changed: Listed via SPAC merger in 2021

name: Amkor Technology
desc: Provides outsourced semiconductor packaging and test services to chip designers and chipmakers.
markets: Chip companies worldwide, with plants in South Korea, Taiwan, Japan, China, Vietnam, Malaysia, Philippines and Portugal.
rationale: B2B service provider with few large customers; little brand need; plausible but not obvious.

name: Applied Optoelectronics
desc: Makes optical networking lasers, transceivers and equipment for data centres, cable broadband and telecom networks.
markets: Hyperscale data centre and cable operators, with manufacturing in the US, Taiwan and China.
rationale: Small B2B optical component supplier with a few concentrated customers and no consumer brand; weak F1 fit.

name: Fortive
desc: Owns industrial technology businesses making test tools, software and workflow products, including Fluke, Tektronix and Accruent.
markets: Industrial, utility, engineering and healthcare customers worldwide, across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Fluke and Tektronix test tools fit an engineering showcase; B2B hospitality value; plausible fit.
changed: Spun out of Danaher in 2016; spun off Ralliant in 2025

name: Forward Industries
desc: Holds Solana digital assets as a treasury strategy and runs a product design and sourcing business.
markets: Few details on customers; the legacy design business served device makers; no verified international activity.
rationale: Crypto treasury vehicle with a small legacy business; crypto peers sponsor F1, but little operating brand; weak fit.
changed: Adopted a Solana treasury strategy in 2025

name: PsiQuantum
desc: Developing a fault-tolerant photonic quantum computer using silicon photonics chips, with sites in Australia and Chicago.
markets: Pre-revenue: building systems in Brisbane, Australia and Chicago with government partners.
rationale: Pre-revenue deep-tech company; technology story is strong but it has no product to sell yet; weak F1 fit.

name: Silicon Box
desc: Provides advanced chiplet integration and panel-level semiconductor packaging for AI, high-performance computing and mobile chips.
markets: Operates a packaging plant in Singapore and is building a plant in Novara, Italy.
rationale: Young B2B manufacturer with few customers; little brand need; weak F1 fit.

name: SiTime
desc: Designs MEMS-based silicon timing chips, including oscillators and clock generators, for electronics makers.
markets: Electronics, data centre, automotive and telecom equipment makers worldwide.
rationale: Precision timing has a neat racing angle, but small B2B company; plausible but not obvious.
changed: Listed on Nasdaq in 2019

name: TTM Technologies
desc: Makes printed circuit boards, RF components and assemblies for aerospace, defence, data centre, automotive and medical customers.
markets: Aerospace, defence, data centre and automotive customers, with plants in North America and Asia.
rationale: B2B circuit board supplier with a defence-heavy business and little brand need; weak F1 fit.

name: OSRAM
desc: Makes LEDs, lasers, optical sensors and automotive lamps for carmakers, electronics firms and consumers.
markets: Carmakers, electronics manufacturers and consumers worldwide, as part of the ams OSRAM group.
rationale: Well-known automotive lighting brand; car-parts marketing fits F1; decision would sit with ams OSRAM.
changed: Acquired by ams in 2020; group now named ams OSRAM

name: REPAY
desc: Provides card and ACH payment processing and bill-pay software for businesses in niche sectors such as consumer lending.
markets: Businesses mainly in the United States; no verified expansion outside North America.
rationale: US-focused B2B payments firm with little consumer brand; weak F1 fit despite payments rivals in the sport.
changed: Listed via SPAC merger with Thunder Bridge in 2019

name: KnowBe4
desc: Provides security awareness training and simulated phishing software, plus email security products, to organisations.
markets: Organisations worldwide, with offices in North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and other regions.
rationale: Cybersecurity rivals CrowdStrike and ThreatLocker sponsor F1; broad B2B customer base suits hospitality and awareness.
changed: Taken private by Vista Equity Partners in 2023; acquired Egress in 2024

name: Legrand
desc: Makes electrical and digital building infrastructure such as switches, sockets, cable management and data centre power products.
markets: Installers, distributors and building owners in nearly 90 countries across Europe, the Americas and Asia.
rationale: Large building-equipment brand with installer marketing; data centre and smart building story; plausible F1 fit.

name: Progress Software
desc: Sells application development, data, content management and file-transfer software, including Telerik, MOVEit and ShareFile.
markets: Developers and businesses worldwide, with offices in North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Enterprise software peers sponsor F1; developer and B2B hospitality angle; plausible but not obvious.
changed: Acquired ShareFile in 2024

name: Alliance Laundry Systems
desc: Makes commercial and home laundry washers and dryers under Speed Queen, UniMac, Huebsch, IPSO and Primus brands.
markets: Laundromats, multi-housing, hotels and institutions in over 100 countries, plus Speed Queen home buyers.
rationale: Speed Queen consumer brand and global B2B distribution; mainly North American consumer reach; plausible fit.
changed: Listed on the NYSE in 2025

name: GoPro
desc: Makes action cameras, mounts and accessories and sells a subscription service for cloud storage and editing.
markets: Consumers and creators worldwide, sold through retailers and online in about 100 countries.
rationale: Action-sports consumer brand built on content; onboard footage and fan content fit F1, though budget is constrained.

name: Advanced Energy Industries
desc: Makes precision power conversion and control systems for semiconductor equipment, industrial, data centre and medical applications.
markets: Equipment makers worldwide, with manufacturing in Asia and operations in North America and Europe.
rationale: B2B power supplier to equipment makers; little brand need; weak to modest F1 fit.

name: ContourGlobal
desc: Owns and operates thermal, hydro, wind and solar power plants, selling electricity under long-term contracts.
markets: Power plants in Europe, Latin America, Africa and the US, selling mainly to utilities and grid operators.
rationale: Wholesale power producer selling under long-term contracts, with no consumer brand to promote; weak F1 fit.
changed: Taken private by KKR in 2022

name: Semtech
desc: Supplies analog and mixed-signal chips, LoRa wireless chips, IoT modules and data centre signal-integrity products.
markets: Electronics makers worldwide in data centre, industrial and consumer markets.
rationale: B2B chip supplier; IoT and connectivity story possible, but modest brand need; plausible but not obvious.
changed: Acquired Sierra Wireless in 2023

name: NextNav
desc: Operates a terrestrial network providing 3D positioning, including floor-level altitude, and backup timing as a GPS alternative.
markets: Wireless carriers, public safety agencies and government in the United States; no verified international operations.
rationale: Small US positioning network company with no consumer brand and limited budget; weak F1 fit.

name: Mirion Technologies
desc: Makes radiation detection, measurement and monitoring products for nuclear power, defence, medical and laboratory customers.
markets: Utilities, hospitals, governments and laboratories worldwide, with operations in North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Niche B2B radiation instruments maker with no consumer brand and little marketing need; weak F1 fit.
changed: Listed via SPAC merger in 2021

name: Enpro Inc.
desc: Makes sealing products, engineered materials and precision components for semiconductor, aerospace, life sciences and industrial customers.
markets: Industrial and semiconductor manufacturers worldwide, with operations in North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: B2B seals and components maker with no consumer brand and little marketing need; weak F1 fit.
changed: Renamed from EnPro Industries to Enpro Inc. in 2023

name: Park Place Technologies
desc: Provides third-party maintenance, hardware support and monitoring for data centre servers, storage and networking equipment.
markets: Enterprise customers in more than 150 countries, with offices in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: IT services peers such as DXC and Cognizant sponsor F1; B2B hospitality with data centre buyers is plausible.

name: Frore Systems
desc: Develops AirJet solid-state active cooling chips for laptops, tablets and other thin devices.
markets: US-based; sells to device makers; international customer details not confirmed.
rationale: Early-stage component supplier with no consumer brand; cooling technology story only; weak F1 fit.

name: Craftsman Automation
desc: Makes precision powertrain and aluminium components, industrial products and storage systems for vehicle and industrial makers.
markets: Mainly Indian vehicle and industrial manufacturers, with some exports.
rationale: Indian auto-parts supplier with little brand marketing; only engineering hospitality with vehicle-maker customers; weak F1 fit.

name: WT Microelectronics
desc: Distributes semiconductors and electronic components from chip suppliers to electronics manufacturers.
markets: Asia-focused, and worldwide since acquiring Canada's Future Electronics with operations in the Americas and Europe.
rationale: Distributor peer Arrow Electronics sponsors F1; B2B hospitality with suppliers and customers; plausible fit.
changed: Acquired Future Electronics in 2024

name: Relativity
desc: Provides RelativityOne, cloud software for e-discovery, investigations and compliance used by law firms, companies and governments.
markets: Law firms, corporations and government bodies mainly in North America, with customers in Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Law-firm peers Ashurst and Morrison Foerster use F1; B2B hospitality for legal clients is plausible.
changed: Founded as kCura; renamed Relativity in 2017

name: SiFive
desc: Designs and licenses RISC-V processor cores and development platforms to chipmakers and system companies.
markets: Chip and system companies in North America, Asia and Europe.
rationale: Processor IP rival Arm sponsors F1; developer and technology angle, but small marketing budget; plausible fit.

name: MatX
desc: Designing AI chips optimised for training and running large language models, for AI labs and cloud providers.
markets: Pre-revenue: chips in development for AI labs and cloud companies; no verified international activity.
rationale: Pre-revenue chip startup with no brand to market yet; weak F1 fit.

name: Nearfield Instruments
desc: Develops atomic force microscopy based metrology and inspection equipment for semiconductor manufacturing.
markets: Sells to chipmakers, which are concentrated in Asia, the US and Europe; customer locations not confirmed.
rationale: Small deep-tech equipment maker selling to a handful of chipmakers, with no brand need; weak F1 fit.

name: Soitec
desc: Makes engineered semiconductor substrates, notably silicon-on-insulator wafers, plus silicon carbide materials for chipmakers.
markets: Chipmakers worldwide, with plants in France and Singapore and customers in Asia, Europe and the US.
rationale: B2B materials supplier with few customers; French technology showcase possible; weak to modest fit.

name: Synchron
desc: Developing the Stentrode, a brain-computer interface implanted through blood vessels to help paralysed people control devices.
markets: Pre-revenue: clinical trials in the United States and Australia; no commercial sales yet.
rationale: Pre-revenue medical device developer with no product to market; weak F1 fit.

name: CentralSquare Technologies
desc: Provides dispatch, records, 911 and jail management software for police, fire, emergency and local government agencies.
markets: Public safety and local government agencies in the United States; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Sells to US government agencies; consumer sponsorship has little value; weak F1 fit.
changed: Formed by merging Superion, TriTech and Zuercher

name: VisionPower Semiconductor Manufacturing Company
desc: Joint venture building a 300mm wafer fab in Singapore to make mature-node chips for automotive and industrial uses.
markets: Pre-revenue: single fab under construction in Singapore, with production expected around 2027.
rationale: Single-fab joint venture with no brand to market; very unlikely F1 sponsor.
changed: Formed in 2024 as a joint venture of Vanguard International Semiconductor and NXP

name: IQM Quantum Computers
desc: Builds superconducting quantum computers and sells on-premises systems and cloud access to research centres and companies.
markets: Supercomputing centres, universities and companies in Europe, with sales and offices in Asia and the US.
rationale: Quantum technology showcase for a European brand; small marketing budget; plausible but not obvious.

name: Winbond Electronics
desc: Designs and makes specialty DRAM, NOR and NAND flash memory chips for automotive, industrial and consumer electronics.
markets: Electronics makers worldwide, with fabs in Taiwan and sales offices in Asia, the US and Europe.
rationale: B2B memory supplier with little brand marketing; weak to modest F1 fit.

name: Bel Fuse
desc: Makes power supplies, magnetics, connectors and circuit protection components for networking, defence, aerospace and industrial equipment.
markets: Equipment makers and distributors worldwide, with factories in Asia, Europe and North America.
rationale: Small B2B electronic component maker with little brand need or consumer exposure; weak F1 fit.
changed: Acquired Enercon Technologies in 2024

name: Exosens
desc: Makes night vision tubes, detectors, cameras and imaging components for defence, industrial, scientific and nuclear customers.
markets: Defence ministries and equipment makers in Europe, North America and other regions.
rationale: Defence-heavy B2B electro-optics maker with no consumer brand and limited marketing need; weak F1 fit.
changed: Renamed from Photonis Group to Exosens in 2023; listed on Euronext Paris in 2024

name: GrafTech International
desc: Makes graphite electrodes for electric arc furnace steelmaking and petroleum needle coke for steel producers.
markets: Steel producers worldwide, with plants in the United States, Mexico, Spain and France.
rationale: Commodity industrial supplier under pricing pressure; little brand need; weak F1 fit.
